title: Choose the visual world — Dental Flower Studio
question: The roll assigned The Herbarium Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Herbarium Sheet
options.lineage: botanical herbarium specimen sheets and their collection labels
options.thesis: Every smile is a specimen cared for individually: pressed, labelled, documented, its own plan.
options.viewport: A white specimen sheet laid on a deep pressed-rose folder: a real Rosa damascena herbarium scan, with the studio name set as the collection label in the corner and a stamped 'Запиши час' as the action.
options.risk: Can tip into museum-cold if the labels are set timidly; warmth has to come from the owner's voice and the rose field.

raised.raise: With phone photos only, type carries whole sections at specimen-label scale, and there are no stock smiles anywhere.
Each treatment is named like a specimen and gets a plain spec line (visits, time, price), so naming never hides the facts.
The label is the summary and the detail unfolds in place (native <details>, no JS).
Sections are sheets laid on the folder, never cards in a grid.
One type family across labels, body and stamps; hierarchy comes from case, size and ink.

options.label: Kazanlak Rose Apothecary
options.thesis: The studio as a Bulgarian rose apothecary, with each treatment a labelled bottle on the shelf.
options.viewport: A rose-madder carton front with a gold-foil studio crest and the plan described as a prescription label.
options.risk: It is the most familiar Bulgarian rose reading, close to the souvenir-shop cosmetics every tourist knows.

options.label: The Treatment Ribbon
options.thesis: One continuous ribbon traces your treatment from the first consultation, through the plan, to regular care.
materials: hairline for the steps still to come
options.viewport: A single rose ribbon runs down the page with the dated plan steps knotted along it.
options.case: It dramatises the individual plan clearly, but patients identify less with a timeline than with care and beauty.
options.risk: Ledger serifs on buff paper slide straight into the cream-editorial default.

options.label: Archive Box Wall
options.thesis: Treatments as stacked boxes, with their names read as poetry.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it reads as retail, not care.
options.kept: Poetic names sit beside plain spec lines.

options.label: Manifesto Page
options.case: Fuses poorly: shouting raises dental anxiety.
options.kept: Type does the work that photography cannot.

options.label: Window-Box Shelf
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is child-facing, and the patients are adults.
options.kept: The front is the summary and the detail opens in place.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern dental clinic site, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A smiling-patient hero with a headline, a booking button and a row of service cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other clinic, and it needs professional photos the studio doesn't have.
